entities.name: Beijing Normal University
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Beijing Normal University (BNU, Beijing Shifan Daxue), founded in 1902 as the Higher Normal School (Shifan Guan) under the Qing dynasty's late educational reforms — making it one of China's oldest modern universities — is China's most important institution for teacher education and educational research, consistently ranked among China's top 10 universities and among the world's top 200, with particular strength in education, psychology, psychology, Chinese language and literature, history, and the natural sciences.

BNU's founding came during the extraordinary period of Chinese educational reform following the Boxer Protocol's requirement that China modernize. The Higher Normal School was established specifically to train teachers in modern subjects, replacing the traditional Confucian examination system that had been abolished in 1905. BNU thus stands at the inflection point of China's educational system — from imperial civil examination to modern universal education.

Through the Republic era, Japanese occupation, the Communist revolution, and the Cultural Revolution (which disrupted BNU's operations as with all Chinese universities), the institution has maintained its central position in Chinese education. Today BNU operates as a comprehensive research university with a distinctive dual identity: excellence in basic and natural sciences (it has produced major research in mathematics, environmental science, and cognitive science) alongside its primary mission of producing China's educational researchers, curriculum designers, and teacher trainers. Its affiliated middle and high school (Beijing Normal University High School) is one of China's most prestigious secondary institutions, producing many of the country's top university entrance scorers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Beijing Normal University — founded in 1902 at China's educational system inflection point from Confucian examinations to modern schooling, training China's teachers and educational researchers across 120+ years, and shaping the education of one-fifth of humanity — is one of the most historically significant educational institutions in the world.
